title: Initial Margin
body: The minimum equity ratio you must put up to open a position on margin. In the US, Reg T typically sets this at 50%; for a $1,000 stock you put in at least $500 and the broker loans the rest. Formula: Required Equity = Position Value × Initial Margin.
example: In the simulator, the "Initial margin %" slider sets this ratio. The required equity at open is derived from it.

title: Maintenance Margin
body: The minimum equity ratio the account must keep while a position is open. The FINRA standard for long positions is 25%; most brokers apply a 25-30% "house" rule. If equity drops below this ratio, a margin call is triggered.
example: At 25% maintenance: a margin call starts the moment Equity < Market Value × 0.25.

title: Margin Call Price
body: The stock price at which the position breaks the maintenance threshold. Formula: Call Price = Debt / (Shares × (1 − Maintenance)). If the price falls below this level you get called: add cash or sell part of the position.
example: The simulator's right panel shows the call price and the distance (buffer) from the current price.

title: Buffer (Resilience Margin)
body: The percentage distance between the current price and the margin call price. A positive buffer means you are safe until prices fall by that much. Zero buffer = you get called at today's price. Negative = already in trouble.
example: The "Margin Buffer" KPI on the dashboard and the warning box in the simulator change color based on buffer status.

title: Collateral Value
body: The contribution your holdings make to your margin capacity. The broker counts only a fraction (haircut) of each stock's value, e.g. 75%. Total available collateral = Cash + ∑(Stock Value × Collateral Rate).
example: On the Portfolio tab you can adjust each stock's collateral rate; this directly affects whether you can open a new trade.

title: Concentration Risk
body: When a single position or sector carries too much weight in the portfolio. Brokers apply extra haircuts to concentrated positions. The product surfaces this in the health score and the finder's sector penalty.
example: If a stock exceeds 40% of the portfolio, a red "Concentrated" label lights up.

title: Carrying Cost
body: The annual interest on the margin debt. A silent eater: even if the price stays flat, daily interest erodes the position. Monthly carry = Debt × Annual Rate / 12.
example: The cost breakdown shows a "Margin interest" line and the flat (0%) scenario in the chart makes this cost visible.

title: Scenario Stress Test
body: Puts the position and the existing portfolio through different market environments at the same time to measure resilience. In scenarios like "Credit Stress" the existing portfolio drops while the trade stays flat — a silent killer.
example: The Scenarios tab shows 8 ready-made scenario cards and the Finder's "worst across all scenarios" mode uses this.
